A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NarrativeFactScore. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original human-correlation and summarization evaluations in Tables 1–2, plus CKG accuracy and post-cutoff evaluations in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds CKG ablations, latency measurements, factual-perturbation results, and a qualitative refinement example.

M1.justification: Both versions use repeated CKG extraction, alias consolidation, frequent relationship selection, retrieval-supported atomic fact checking, and iterative refinement. v2 expands the explanation and notation without establishing a changed procedure. The operational prompts in Appendix D.1–D.5 are unchanged.

E1.justification: STORYSUMM, FABLES, MENSA, MovieSum, Conan, and the 18-film post-cutoff subset are retained. v2 adds deliberately corrupted MENSA reference summaries as a distinct evaluation condition in Section 5.5; it adds no new underlying corpus or domain.

E2.justification: v2 Table 2 introduces single-step-CKG and no-CKG variants as explicit comparators in human-correlation evaluation. The external comparator sets in the existing correlation, summarization, and Conan comparisons remain unchanged; revised FActScore scores do not establish a changed baseline method.

E3.justification: v2 substantially expands evaluation design with CKG component controls, separate extraction and factuality timing, and paired reference-versus-perturbed summaries generated through minimal GPT-4o word replacements. Existing benchmark sample counts, model configuration, retrieval settings, and refinement budgets are retained.

E4.justification: New analyses test whether graph consistency matters for human agreement (Table 2), whether metrics detect factual perturbations (Table 8), and the latency cost of evaluation (Table 7). Appendix A adds a detailed error-and-refinement case study. The Conan and post-cutoff analyses already existed in v1's appendix.

E5.justification: v1's exact p-value of 0.00003 is replaced by statements that p-values are below 0.05 for all datasets. This changes reporting specificity and explicitly states dataset coverage, without establishing new tests or runs. Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run uncertainty, or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes FActScore's Spearman/Kendall values from 0.30/0.21 to 0.19/0.13 on STORYSUMM and from 0.25/0.16 to 0.16/0.09 on FABLES; NFS values remain unchanged. v2 adds ablation, latency, perturbation, and qualitative outcomes. Its new perturbation test reports NFS of 95.42 for reference summaries and 40.81 for perturbed summaries. Retained summarization, Conan, and post-cutoff table values are identical.

T1.justification: v2 Section 5.1 introduces a bivariate-normality assumption for converting Kendall interpretation intervals into Spearman intervals in Table 4; v1 only supplied Kendall cutoffs. The added graph and indicator equations largely formalize the existing procedure, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: v2's abstract adds explicit claims of being the first narrative Agent-as-a-Judge framework, using one-third of prior factuality computation, and achieving threefold human correlation. These materially strengthen the central novelty and efficiency claims beyond v1's general superiority claim. The main summarization improvement claims are retained.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations that inconsistent graphs can perform worse than no graph, graph reasoning trades latency for accuracy, and NFS is sensitive to factual perturbations. Section 7 newly identifies irrelevant subgraph retrieval and unverified generalization beyond narratives as limitations. v1's discussion of refinement saturation is removed.

D1.justification: v2 discloses an NVIDIA RTX 3090 for retrieval and supplies the GPT-4o factual-perturbation prompt in Appendix D.6. The embedded demo link changes to an anonymized Hugging Face space. Existing model, chunk-size, and retrieval details are retained after relocation; the code reference is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Botsch (2011) for correlation interpretation and Bradley Brown et al. (2024) for repeated sampling. It strengthens novelty positioning through the first-framework claim, while retaining the earlier cited works and largely unchanged related-work discussion.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the paper: implementation details and appendix analyses enter the main text, while the demonstration becomes an appendix deployment discussion. The abstract and several introduction/method paragraphs are rewritten, and limitations, a qualitative example, and an AI-writing disclosure are added.

P2.justification: v2 adds five tables and the factual-perturbation prompt figure. Figure 3 revises relationship and character-state labels, existing result tables are relocated and reformatted, and Table 1 adds correlation highlighting. Figure 4 retains the same screenshots with revised sizing and caption.

improvement.justification: The added ablations, perturbation test, and explicit limitations strengthen validation beyond v1. However, the new one-third-computation claim is unsupported by its cited latency evidence: Table 7 reports 1.17 minutes for CKG extraction plus 4.81 for checking, versus 3.81 and 4.60 for competing metrics. FActScore's lower correlations are also unexplained while NFS scores remain fixed. These unresolved reporting problems make the net benefit of the added evidence uncertain.
